messages.author: c6ca7877bef91eef
messages.subject: DataTables and Shiny
parts:
Folks,

rCharts now supports DataTables. You can create DataTables from a data frame either for a static html page or for a Shiny application.

Here is a gist with a minimal example of a Shiny App using rCharts to create DataTables.

https://gist.github.com/ramnathv/8232949d68c3402e398d

You can view the application here

http://glimmer.rstudio.com/ramnathv/datatables/

DataTables has several configuration parameters and the rCharts wrapper to DataTables exposes all of them, so that you can customize your application easily.

If you have suggestions/comments/feedback, please post them on the github page for rCharts.

Best,
Ramnath

messages.author: c6ca7877bef91eef
messages.subject: Re: DataTables and Shiny
parts:
You can handle it just like sPaginationType. The key is to make sure that the R representation of the object results in the correct JSON. For example.

mytable <- dTable(iris, aaSorting = list(c(1, "desc")))

would display the table sorted descending on the first column.

If you do toJSON(list(c(1, "desc"))), you will get [[1, "desc"]].  So when in doubt, use fromJSON to figure out the correct representation in R.

I am toying with the idea of allowing configuration parameters to be input as either R objects or JSON directly, in which case, you could just copy the JSON required. But, this is scheduled for a later version.

Let me know if this addresses your question.

Greetings Ramnath,

I really like the data tables you have created and I have been using them in my applications- however I was almost ready to submit the shiny app I had been working on as 'final' when I noticed something strange in the details- the sorting of data in columns in regards to scientific notation.  Unfortunately, this is an example of the sorting:

7.07e-40
6.37e-7
4.06e-32

The issue is that 7.07e-40 is by far the smallest number here (it is very close to zero, it is 0.(40 zeros)707, but it is listed as the largest because 7>6.  And in terms of my program, p values indicate the likelihood of the results being statistically significant, and the closer to 0 they are, the better, so this issue is rather concerning for the sorting.

Is there an option for having data tables take into account scientific notation?  Otherwise I suspect the work around would be to create a 'rank' column for each column which has their data in scientific notation.  Just wanted to check first. 

Thanks,
Mike
